title: Emergency water storage
aliases: how much water should i store
tldr: Store at least one gallon of water per person per day for three days; aim for two weeks if practical. Allow more for heat, illness, pregnancy and pets. Use commercially bottled water or clean food-grade containers, and keep it cool and away from chemicals.
steps: Count people and days and add water for pets and extra needs.
Use commercially bottled water or food-grade containers intended for water.
Mark fill dates and store away from sunlight, fuel and cleaning products.
Follow bottled-water dates and replace self-filled stored water every six months.
next: Learn the local advisory system. Plan how to transport water if distribution sites open.
watch: Do not reuse containers that held toxic substances, even after washing.
shopping: Commercially bottled water or food-grade storage containers

scope: Civilian educational guidance. Linked references may use U.S. emergency systems; local warning methods, laws, services and conditions differ.
sections: Plan at least one gallon per person per day for drinking and basic sanitation, with additional water for heat, pregnancy, illness and other needs. Add pets and any equipment requirements. A three-day supply is a starting point; expand within safe space and budget rather than promising that a fixed amount covers every household.

Use suitable food-grade containers and follow CDC cleaning and filling guidance. Label filled containers and avoid heat, direct sunlight and chemicals. Replace self-filled stored water every six months; follow commercially bottled water labeling. Practice pouring without contaminating the container or sharing a drinking utensil.
Make the reserve easy to use

Editorial layout: keep drinking water separate from cleaning supplies, label the storage or purchase date, and identify the container you will open first. Test whether the person with the least strength can lift or dispense it. Distribute the reserve so one leak or inaccessible cupboard does not remove the entire supply.
